category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your wedding was scheduled the same day as the Georgia-Florida game. Explain to your fiancée why the venue has TVs now.
response:
Babe, I love you more than anything in this world, and I swear I didn't plan this... but the venue just called me back and said they "had a change in policy."

They're installing flat-screens. Plural.

Apparently some other groom a few years ago had a full-on meltdown during the cocktail hour when he found out he was missing the Georgia-Florida game, so now it's just... venue policy. They put TVs in the reception hall "for the comfort and happiness of all guests." Their words, not mine.

Look, I know this is our wedding day. I know it's sacred. But hear me out:

1. Half our guest list is either from Athens or Jacksonville. These people have been bleeding red and black or orange and blue since birth. If we make them choose between our vows and the Cocktail Party, we're going to have some very emotionally conflicted humans in the pews.

2. The game is at 3:30. Our ceremony is at 2. If we time the reception right, the only thing they'll actually miss is the pre-game show. We get married, say "I do," take pictures, and by the time we walk into the reception the game is just getting started. It's... almost like the universe scheduled this.

3. I'll make a deal with you. We can mute the TVs during the ceremony (obviously) and during our first dance. But once the cake is cut? Just let the people have their emotional support football. I'll even put it in the vows if you want.

   "I, [Your Name], promise to love, honor, and not scream at the ref while we're cutting the cake."

I already told them to put one TV near the bar and one near the dessert table so people aren't all clustered in one spot like animals. The venue swears the TVs are tasteful. They're even going to decorate around them with our flowers so it doesn't look like we turned our wedding into a sports bar.

Baby... this is the only way we get both. Our perfect day AND the Gators getting what they deserve.

What do you say? For us?

...And for the sanity of every man over 40 who's attending?
